data.title: High quality, low risk: record number of Japanese in Premier League
data.description: TOKYO - A record number of Japanese players are in England's Premier League this season, with clubs attracted by their proven quality, value for money and the "very little risk" involved in signing them.

data.title: Fave or flop? A guide to gauging video game success
data.description: COLOGNE (GERMANY) - The video game industry is notoriously tight-lipped about its numbers, filled with members-only metrics like wishlists, pre-orders and player numbers, so it can be hard to know which games have actually proven popular and turned a profit.

data.title: PGA chief says 'no current plans' for LIV stars to return
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said on Tuesday.

data.title: Golf giant Callaway apologises after ad sparks outcry
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert, which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver.

data.title: Instagram chief admits touting teen safety tool while omitting it was barely used
data.description: OAKLAND (UNITED STATES) - Adam Mosseri, who oversees Instagram at Meta, admitted in a California court on Tuesday that he touted newly launched safety tools for teens without disclosing low adoption rates from early testing several years ago.

data.title: Social media use on the rise among Australian under-16s after ban: data
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian under-16s are increasing their use of social media apps such as Instagram and Tiktok despite a world-leading ban, data provided by a parental control software company showed on Wednesday.

data.title: Syrian Kurdish leader dissolves force that spearheaded jihadist fight
data.description: DAMASCUS - The leader of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, the Washington-backed group at the forefront of the battle against the Islamic State jihadist group, announced their dissolution on Tuesday under a deal with the government.

data.title: Canada hits back against Trump’s steep tariffs
data.description: OTTAWA - Canada on Tuesday announced counter-tariffs on US goods ranging between 15% and 50%, intensifying the trade war between the historically close allies.

data.title: Climate change becomes a scorching reality for Europe
data.description: PARIS - For generations, summer in Europe has been languid and dreamy, bringing fine weather and lengthy days on sunny beaches and terraces. But in 2026, the brutal reality of climate change forced its way into daily life.

data.title: Spain speeds up return of migrants from Ceuta
data.description: MADRID - Spain’s government took steps on Tuesday to speed up the return of thousands of migrants still in the Spanish territory of Ceuta following a mass influx from Morocco in July.

data.title: Iranians queue for petrol as US announces new sanctions
data.description: TEHRAN - Long queues formed at petrol stations in Tehran on Tuesday after the United States announced fresh sanctions aimed at pressuring Iran into submission.

data.title: Myanmar human rights conditions at new low, UN says
data.description: GENEVA - Human rights conditions in Myanmar have ‌sunk to a new low, with widespread abuses against the Rohingya minority and a booming illicit economy driven partly by illegal rare-earth mining deepening civilian suffering, the United Nations said on Tuesday.

data.title: Canada ready to respond to Trump’s steep tariffs
data.description: Canada is preparing to announce its answer to US President Donald Trump's latest wave of tariffs on Tuesday, as a trade war intensifies between the historically close allies

data.title: UN: One million Afghan children face ‘life-threatening’ malnutrition
data.description: GENEVA - One million children in Afghanistan are suffering from life-threatening malnutrition in a worsening new crisis hitting the country, the United Nations warned on Tuesday.

data.title: West Bank settlers attack AFP journalists
data.description: JANNATAH, Palestinian Territories - Israeli settlers in the West Bank on Tuesday attacked AFP journalists reporting on tension with Palestinians, in violence that left at least five people injured, the reporters and medics said.

data.title: World urged to rein in ‘killer robots’
data.description: GENEVA - The United Nations and the Red Cross warned Tuesday that the world is “dangerously close” to a future where so-called “killer robots” could target humans, and issued an urgent appeal for international regulation of autonomous weapons.

data.title: Europe's gaming bash kicks off as industry eyes 'Grand Theft' boost
data.description: COLOGNE (GERMANY) - Europe's biggest video games show Gamescom opens its doors Tuesday in Cologne with the industry hoping that the coming blockbuster "Grand Theft Auto VI" can provide a much-needed boost, as studios cut jobs amid fierce competition.

data.title: One million Afghan children suffering 'life-threatening' malnutrition: UN
data.description: GENEVA - One million children in Afghanistan are suffering from life-threatening malnutrition in a worsening new crisis hitting the country, the United Nations warned Tuesday.

data.title: Lockerbie bombing trial delayed over ‘new evidence’
data.description: WASHINGTON - A US federal judge has postponed the trial of a Libyan man accused of making the bomb that destroyed a Pan Am flight over Scotland in 1988, killing 270 people, citing new evidence.

data.title: ‘Traumatic’ tornado shatters French village
data.description: POMAS, France - Two people were in critical condition and thousands of households were without power on Tuesday after a “tornado of severe intensity” wreaked havoc in southern France, officials said.

data.title: Trees 'giving up': climate change hammers historic English gardens
data.description: HAMPTON COURT (UNITED KINGDOM) - At Hampton Court Palace, head gardener Graham Dillamore strode across the burnt beige grass in the spectacular formal gardens southwest of London, laid out in the 17th century.

data.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
data.description: WINDHOEK — Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry.

data.title: Florida opens a dedicated Jellyfish Museum
data.description: Right on the coast of Florida, Pompano Beach has opened a new venture dedicated to one of the ocean’s most enigmatic creatures: the jellyfish, a boneless and brainless invertebrate that has survived in the earth’s ocean for over 500 million years.

data.title: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.

data.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
data.description: TOKYO — Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.

data.title: Trump veers from boredom to denial after six months of Iran war
data.description: WASHINGTON — At an impromptu press conference last week, US President Donald Trump waxed lyrical about his helipad, his ballroom and his granite paving stones.

data.title: Families of detained Chinese Christians cling to faith in legal limbo
data.description: BEIHAI — Clasping her hands together in prayer, four-year-old Huanle tells God she misses her mum, whom she has not seen since Chinese authorities raided their home last year in a crackdown on their unregistered church.

data.title: Tens of thousands flee fire near US city of Reno
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - Tens of thousands of people looked set to spend another night away from home Monday as a wind-driven fire bore down on the western US city of Reno.

data.title: US proposes expanding UN Sudan arms embargo to entire country
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The United States proposed at the UN on Monday to expand an arms embargo on the Sudanese region of Darfur to cover all of Sudan, saying the nation's brutal conflict risks regional expansion.

data.title: Ceasefire verification mission heads to east DR Congo
data.description: KINSHASA - A mission to verify a fragile ceasefire between the Congolese army and Rwanda-backed M23 armed group was deployed Monday to the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the two sides traded accusations of abuse.

data.title: US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The United States on Monday removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that came with severe economic restrictions and marking another step in warming ties between the countries.

data.title: Trump says to double tariffs on Canada autos as trade fight heats up
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Monday that he would double tariffs on Canadian vehicles beginning next year, as the neighboring countries spiral towards an escalating trade war.

data.title: France readies high school phone ban for next month
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The French government said Monday it would press ahead with a ban on mobile phones in high schools from next month, but trade unions warned that the measure might be hard to implement quickly.

data.title: French poll shows Le Pen's biggest challenger may be hard left's Melenchon
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon may have the best chance of reaching the run-off against far-right leader Marine Le Pen in next spring's election, a new poll showed Monday, underscoring the increasingly polarised nature of the race.

data.title: Empire State Building climbers kiss outside court after viral proposal
data.description: NEW YORK - A couple who climbed to the top of the Empire State Building and got engaged appeared in a New York court Monday, before giving each other a lingering kiss in full view of the world's media.

data.title: British PM Burnham hits a chord on Kyiv visit
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Monday strummed on a guitar and also went to a shopping mall destroyed by a Russian strike as he visited Kyiv to show his country's support for Ukraine.

data.title: Saudi Arabia to invest $7 bn in theme parks near Paris: French presidency
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding for a six-billion-euro ($7 billion) Saudi investment to create three theme parks near Paris, including one likely to be manga-themed, the office of the French president said.
